title: Japan's Latest Tourism Trend: Getting Better Sleep
paragraphs: When you stay at a hotel, you might look forward to the food, the view, or maybe a nice room — or the hotel pool!
But what if the main reason for your stay was just to get a really good night's sleep?
That idea is becoming popular in Japan, as more hotels are offering "sleep tourism" experiences, with special services to help tired travelers sleep better.
For example, Hotel 1899 Tokyo starts by asking a few simple questions about how you sleep. Based on your answers, the hotel chooses a special blend of tea for you.
Then, once you're in your room, you'll find special pillows, bath salts and incense to help you relax.
A spokesperson for the hotel told The Mainichi the idea came from a simple fact — guests spend a large part of their hotel stay sleeping!
Other hotels are using technology to help guests get a better night's sleep.
At Hotel Chinzanso Tokyo, guests can put a thin device on their foreheads to check their brain waves while they sleep. The device can show information such as how long it took them to fall asleep.
Guests can then talk to doctors at the hotel's clinic and get advice based on the data.
Hotels outside Tokyo are offering sleep experiences too.
At Malibu Hotel in Kanagawa, the focus is on the bed itself. Its "Sleep Well Stay" plan gives guests bedding chosen for the way they sleep.
Guests answer questions about their sleep, including the position they usually sleep in. The hotel then uses their answers to choose the perfect mattress and other bedding for them.
For some travelers in Japan, a hotel is becoming more than just a place to stay while they travel — getting a really good night's sleep is becoming part of the experience itself!
